# gh-1503: [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only

## Description

## Problem

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

Port the #1471 design onto `bench-harbor.yml`, reusing the exact same mapping (single source — extract the resolve step into a composite action or shared script if that kills the duplication; otherwise a byte-consistent copy with a cross-reference comment in both files):

1. `provider` choice input (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`) + `provider-config` for custom — same semantics, same validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-looking fields, jq-parse hard-fail).
2. kimi maps to type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384, key env from `secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`.
3. Preflight: selected provider's secret missing → fail in the first minute (today only the zai key is checked at :264).
4. Run identity: workflow/job names + summary carry provider+model (bench.yml pattern: `fa bench · <provider> · <model>`); the free-text `model` input becomes derived-from-provider (keep it as override only for `custom`, or drop it if redundant).
5. REG: default dispatch (no provider input) resolves byte-identical to today's zai glm wiring.
6. `n-concurrent` default is 1 ("z.ai rate-limit safe") — keep for zai; document the kimi-safe value in the input description (kimi coding plan tolerates more; owner picks at dispatch).

## Acceptance

- `bench-harbor.yml` dispatchable with `provider=kimi-for-coding`; smoke run (one task, e.g. the family smoke per docs/bench.md) green on TB 2.1 with kimi.
- actionlint + the workflow-shape tests extended for the new inputs/mapping (mirror of #1475's tests).
- Default-path REG green.

## References

- #1471 (design), PR #1475 (bench.yml implementation to mirror)
- bench-harbor.yml:247-264 (current hardcode)
- kimi wiring precedent: ~/.fah/config.yaml custom providers (apiType kimi, k3-256k)

# gh-1503: [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only

## Description

## Problem

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

Port the #1471 design onto `bench-harbor.yml`, reusing the exact same mapping (single source — extract the resolve step into a composite action or shared script if that kills the duplication; otherwise a byte-consistent copy with a cross-reference comment in both files):

1. `provider` choice input (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`) + `provider-config` for custom — same semantics, same validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-looking fields, jq-parse hard-fail).
2. kimi maps to type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384, key env from `secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`.
3. Preflight: selected provider's secret missing → fail in the first minute (today only the zai key is checked at :264).
4. Run identity: workflow/job names + summary carry provider+model (bench.yml pattern: `fa bench · <provider> · <model>`); the free-text `model` input becomes derived-from-provider (keep it as override only for `custom`, or drop it if redundant).
5. REG: default dispatch (no provider input) resolves byte-identical to today's zai glm wiring.
6. `n-concurrent` default is 1 ("z.ai rate-limit safe") — keep for zai; document the kimi-safe value in the input description (kimi coding plan tolerates more; owner picks at dispatch).

## Acceptance

- `bench-harbor.yml` dispatchable with `provider=kimi-for-coding`; smoke run (one task, e.g. the family smoke per docs/bench.md) green on TB 2.1 with kimi.
- actionlint + the workflow-shape tests extended for the new inputs/mapping (mirror of #1475's tests).
- Default-path REG green.

## References

- #1471 (design), PR #1475 (bench.yml implementation to mirror)
- bench-harbor.yml:247-264 (current hardcode)
- kimi wiring precedent: ~/.fah/config.yaml custom providers (apiType kimi, k3-256k)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1505
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1505
- **Title**: gh-1503 [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1503` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +713
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:10:58Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:35:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #1503
## What changed

Ported the gh-1471 provider selection onto `bench-harbor.yml` (TB 2.x/Harbor path): a setup-job **Resolve provider** step maps the new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom` + `provider-config`) to the full provider triple and preflights the selected secret before any shard starts. The free-text `model` input is dropped — the model is derived from the provider.

## Key decisions

- **Byte-consistent copy, not extraction**: the resolve step's `run:` block is byte-identical to `bench.yml`'s (verified by a test); cross-reference comments in both files are the sync contract (single-source extraction was rejected to keep the workflows self-contained, same call gh-1471 made).
- **REG-1**: default dispatch resolves the exact 3-field zai JSON the workflow hardcoded pre-change (pinned in tests).
- **kimi** maps to type `kimi`, `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000 / maxTokens 16384, key from `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`; `custom` gets the full gh-1471 validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-like fields at any depth, Dart preconfig contract mirror).
- **Run identity**: `run-name: fa bench-harbor · <provider> · <tasks>`, shard job name carries `run_label`, summary gets `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` (`bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` gained the gh-1471-style `Provider:` line).
- **Defense in depth**: shard run block resolves the key by name via `FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV` indirection (same as bench.yml).
- `n-concurrent` default stays `1`; the kimi-safe guidance lives in the input description.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa   # 58 tests, incl. the mirrored resolve-block suite
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench  # 345 tests, bench.yml REG green

# gh-1503: [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only

## Description

## Problem

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

Port the #1471 design onto `bench-harbor.yml`, reusing the exact same mapping (single source — extract the resolve step into a composite action or shared script if that kills the duplication; otherwise a byte-consistent copy with a cross-reference comment in both files):

1. `provider` choice input (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`) + `provider-config` for custom — same semantics, same validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-looking fields, jq-parse hard-fail).
2. kimi maps to type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384, key env from `secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`.
3. Preflight: selected provider's secret missing → fail in the first minute (today only the zai key is checked at :264).
4. Run identity: workflow/job names + summary carry provider+model (bench.yml pattern: `fa bench · <provider> · <model>`); the free-text `model` input becomes derived-from-provider (keep it as override only for `custom`, or drop it if redundant).
5. REG: default dispatch (no provider input) resolves byte-identical to today's zai glm wiring.
6. `n-concurrent` default is 1 ("z.ai rate-limit safe") — keep for zai; document the kimi-safe value in the input description (kimi coding plan tolerates more; owner picks at dispatch).

## Acceptance

- `bench-harbor.yml` dispatchable with `provider=kimi-for-coding`; smoke run (one task, e.g. the family smoke per docs/bench.md) green on TB 2.1 with kimi.
- actionlint + the workflow-shape tests extended for the new inputs/mapping (mirror of #1475's tests).
- Default-path REG green.

## References

- #1471 (design), PR #1475 (bench.yml implementation to mirror)
- bench-harbor.yml:247-264 (current hardcode)
- kimi wiring precedent: ~/.fah/config.yaml custom providers (apiType kimi, k3-256k)

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1505
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1505
- **Title**: gh-1503 [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1503` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +713
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:10:58Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:35:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #1503
## What changed

Ported the gh-1471 provider selection onto `bench-harbor.yml` (TB 2.x/Harbor path): a setup-job **Resolve provider** step maps the new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom` + `provider-config`) to the full provider triple and preflights the selected secret before any shard starts. The free-text `model` input is dropped — the model is derived from the provider.

## Key decisions

- **Byte-consistent copy, not extraction**: the resolve step's `run:` block is byte-identical to `bench.yml`'s (verified by a test); cross-reference comments in both files are the sync contract (single-source extraction was rejected to keep the workflows self-contained, same call gh-1471 made).
- **REG-1**: default dispatch resolves the exact 3-field zai JSON the workflow hardcoded pre-change (pinned in tests).
- **kimi** maps to type `kimi`, `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000 / maxTokens 16384, key from `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`; `custom` gets the full gh-1471 validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-like fields at any depth, Dart preconfig contract mirror).
- **Run identity**: `run-name: fa bench-harbor · <provider> · <tasks>`, shard job name carries `run_label`, summary gets `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` (`bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` gained the gh-1471-style `Provider:` line).
- **Defense in depth**: shard run block resolves the key by name via `FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV` indirection (same as bench.yml).
- `n-concurrent` default stays `1`; the kimi-safe guidance lives in the input description.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa   # 58 tests, incl. the mirrored resolve-block suite
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench  # 345 tests, bench.yml REG green
actionlint .github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml  # only 3 pre-existing findings (inputs.model one fixed)
```

Note: live smoke (`provider=kimi-for-coding`, one 2.1 family smoke task, `attempts: 1`) still requires the `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret and a real dispatch — not runnable from this runner.

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  D[workflow_dispatch provider] --> S[setup: Resolve provider]
  S -->|zai default| Z["zai glm-5.3-flash (byte-identical)"]
  S -->|kimi-for-coding| K["kimi k3-256k + caps"]
  S -->|custom| C["validated provider-config JSON"]
  S -->|missing secret| E[::error in first minute]
  S --> O["outputs: type/config/key_env/bench_model/run_label"]
  O --> B["shard env: FA_PROVIDER_* + 3 key mappings"]
  B --> R["run block picks key by name (indirection)"]
  O --> M["job name + summary: BENCH_RUN_LABEL"]
```

</details>

# gh-1503: [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only

## Description

## Problem

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

Port the #1471 design onto `bench-harbor.yml`, reusing the exact same mapping (single source — extract the resolve step into a composite action or shared script if that kills the duplication; otherwise a byte-consistent copy with a cross-reference comment in both files):

1. `provider` choice input (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`) + `provider-config` for custom — same semantics, same validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-looking fields, jq-parse hard-fail).
2. kimi maps to type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384, key env from `secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`.
3. Preflight: selected provider's secret missing → fail in the first minute (today only the zai key is checked at :264).
4. Run identity: workflow/job names + summary carry provider+model (bench.yml pattern: `fa bench · <provider> · <model>`); the free-text `model` input becomes derived-from-provider (keep it as override only for `custom`, or drop it if redundant).
5. REG: default dispatch (no provider input) resolves byte-identical to today's zai glm wiring.
6. `n-concurrent` default is 1 ("z.ai rate-limit safe") — keep for zai; document the kimi-safe value in the input description (kimi coding plan tolerates more; owner picks at dispatch).

## Acceptance

- `bench-harbor.yml` dispatchable with `provider=kimi-for-coding`; smoke run (one task, e.g. the family smoke per docs/bench.md) green on TB 2.1 with kimi.
- actionlint + the workflow-shape tests extended for the new inputs/mapping (mirror of #1475's tests).
- Default-path REG green.

## References

- #1471 (design), PR #1475 (bench.yml implementation to mirror)
- bench-harbor.yml:247-264 (current hardcode)
- kimi wiring precedent: ~/.fah/config.yaml custom providers (apiType kimi, k3-256k)

Read input context:

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1505
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1505
- **Title**: gh-1503 [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1503` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +713
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:10:58Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:35:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #1503
## What changed

Ported the gh-1471 provider selection onto `bench-harbor.yml` (TB 2.x/Harbor path): a setup-job **Resolve provider** step maps the new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom` + `provider-config`) to the full provider triple and preflights the selected secret before any shard starts. The free-text `model` input is dropped — the model is derived from the provider.

## Key decisions

- **Byte-consistent copy, not extraction**: the resolve step's `run:` block is byte-identical to `bench.yml`'s (verified by a test); cross-reference comments in both files are the sync contract (single-source extraction was rejected to keep the workflows self-contained, same call gh-1471 made).
- **REG-1**: default dispatch resolves the exact 3-field zai JSON the workflow hardcoded pre-change (pinned in tests).
- **kimi** maps to type `kimi`, `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000 / maxTokens 16384, key from `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`; `custom` gets the full gh-1471 validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-like fields at any depth, Dart preconfig contract mirror).
- **Run identity**: `run-name: fa bench-harbor · <provider> · <tasks>`, shard job name carries `run_label`, summary gets `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` (`bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` gained the gh-1471-style `Provider:` line).
- **Defense in depth**: shard run block resolves the key by name via `FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV` indirection (same as bench.yml).

# gh-1503: [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only

## Description

## Problem

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

Port the #1471 design onto `bench-harbor.yml`, reusing the exact same mapping (single source — extract the resolve step into a composite action or shared script if that kills the duplication; otherwise a byte-consistent copy with a cross-reference comment in both files):

1. `provider` choice input (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`) + `provider-config` for custom — same semantics, same validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-looking fields, jq-parse hard-fail).
2. kimi maps to type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384, key env from `secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`.
3. Preflight: selected provider's secret missing → fail in the first minute (today only the zai key is checked at :264).
4. Run identity: workflow/job names + summary carry provider+model (bench.yml pattern: `fa bench · <provider> · <model>`); the free-text `model` input becomes derived-from-provider (keep it as override only for `custom`, or drop it if redundant).
5. REG: default dispatch (no provider input) resolves byte-identical to today's zai glm wiring.
6. `n-concurrent` default is 1 ("z.ai rate-limit safe") — keep for zai; document the kimi-safe value in the input description (kimi coding plan tolerates more; owner picks at dispatch).

## Acceptance

- `bench-harbor.yml` dispatchable with `provider=kimi-for-coding`; smoke run (one task, e.g. the family smoke per docs/bench.md) green on TB 2.1 with kimi.
- actionlint + the workflow-shape tests extended for the new inputs/mapping (mirror of #1475's tests).
- Default-path REG green.

- #1471 (design), PR #1475 (bench.yml implementation to mirror)
- bench-harbor.yml:247-264 (current hardcode)
- kimi wiring precedent: ~/.fah/config.yaml custom providers (apiType kimi, k3-256k)

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      # gh-1503: bench-harbor.yml carries a byte-consistent copy of this
      # step's run block (same inputs, same outputs) — keep both in sync;
      # the cross-reference comment in both files is the sync contract.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Closes #1503
## What changed

Ported the gh-1471 provider selection onto `bench-harbor.yml` (TB 2.x/Harbor path): a setup-job **Resolve provider** step maps the new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom` + `provider-config`) to the full provider triple and preflights the selected secret before any shard starts. The free-text `model` input is dropped — the model is derived from the provider.

## Key decisions

- **Byte-consistent copy, not extraction**: the resolve step's `run:` block is byte-identical to `bench.yml`'s (verified by a test); cross-reference comments in both files are the sync contract (single-source extraction was rejected to keep the workflows self-contained, same call gh-1471 made).
- **REG-1**: default dispatch resolves the exact 3-field zai JSON the workflow hardcoded pre-change (pinned in tests).
- **kimi** maps to type `kimi`, `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000 / maxTokens 16384, key from `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`; `custom` gets the full gh-1471 validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-like fields at any depth, Dart preconfig contract mirror).

# gh-1503: [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only

## Description

## Problem

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      # gh-1503: bench-harbor.yml carries a byte-consistent copy of this
      # step's run block (same inputs, same outputs) — keep both in sync;
      # the cross-reference comment in both files is the sync contract.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}

          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

  bench:
    name: fa on tbench ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench agent caps
    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    env:
      FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
      DATASET: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      # The optional self-hosted runner is a macOS box: setup-python cannot
      # write the hosted tool cache there (mkdir /Users/runner denied) and the
      # runner's own python3 is 3.14 — typer-based CLIs (harbor) break on 3.14.
      # The uv-managed CPython 3.13 user-space install below works on BOTH
      # runner kinds (the ubuntu-latest default included); uv is also the
      # canonical harbor install per the 4.0 docs.
      - name: Install harbor (uv-managed python 3.13)
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          uv venv --python 3.13 .bench-venv
          uv pip install --python .bench-venv/bin/python 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
          .bench-venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print("venv python:", sys.version.split()[0])'

      - name: Run harbor (fa agent, ${{ matrix.env }} env)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/harbor_fa
          # gh-1503: the provider triple is resolved once in the setup
          # job (preflighted secret + hard fail on an unmapped choice) —
          # the shard only consumes it. All three bench keys are mapped
          # here (custom's AC 2a: key only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY); the
          # run block picks the resolved one by name, fa_agent.py ships
          # exactly that key into the container.
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_type }}
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_config }}
          FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_key_env }}
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_ID: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_ID }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET }}
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          NCONC: ${{ inputs.n-concurrent }}
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py); absent inputs stay byte-for-byte
          # today's run (REG-1). A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # Pinned --job-name: one jobs/<name>/ dir per shard, so the summary
          # job's downloads cannot collide on harbor's timestamped default.
          # The family label keys results per dataset version (fa-4.0-*
          # matches the historical 4.0 names exactly).
          .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
            -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
            --job-name "fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${{ matrix.kind }}-${{ matrix.i }}" -o jobs \
            "${args[@]}"

      - name: Upload harbor job (shard ${{ matrix.i }})
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: harbor-job-shard-${{ matrix.i }}
          path: jobs/

      - name: Upload to Harbor Hub
        if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''
        env:
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          for job_dir in jobs/fa-${FAMILY}-*; do
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor upload "$job_dir" --public
          done

  summary:
    name: Aggregate resolution rate
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: harbor-job-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: jobs

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          # gh-1503: pinned to the setup resolve step's outputs — the
          # free-text model input is gone; provider+model is derived
          # from the provider choice (same contract as bench.yml).
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1503: the report names the provider+model — glm and kimi
          # runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" jobs

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1505
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1505
- **Title**: gh-1503 [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1503` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +713
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:10:58Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:35:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #1503
## What changed

Ported the gh-1471 provider selection onto `bench-harbor.yml` (TB 2.x/Harbor path): a setup-job **Resolve provider** step maps the new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom` + `provider-config`) to the full provider triple and preflights the selected secret before any shard starts. The free-text `model` input is dropped — the model is derived from the provider.

## Key decisions

- **Byte-consistent copy, not extraction**: the resolve step's `run:` block is byte-identical to `bench.yml`'s (verified by a test); cross-reference comments in both files are the sync contract (single-source extraction was rejected to keep the workflows self-contained, same call gh-1471 made).
- **REG-1**: default dispatch resolves the exact 3-field zai JSON the workflow hardcoded pre-change (pinned in tests).
- **kimi** maps to type `kimi`, `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000 / maxTokens 16384, key from `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`; `custom` gets the full gh-1471 validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-like fields at any depth, Dart preconfig contract mirror).
- **Run identity**: `run-name: fa bench-harbor · <provider> · <tasks>`, shard job name carries `run_label`, summary gets `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` (`bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` gained the gh-1471-style `Provider:` line).
- **Defense in depth**: shard run block resolves the key by name via `FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV` indirection (same as bench.yml).
- `n-concurrent` default stays `1`; the kimi-safe guidance lives in the input description.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa   # 58 tests, incl. the mirrored resolve-block suite
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench  # 345 tests, bench.yml REG green
actionlint .github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml  # only 3 pre-existing findings (inputs.model one fixed)
```

Note: live smoke (`provider=kimi-for-coding`, one 2.1 family smoke task, `attempts: 1`) still requires the `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret and a real dispatch — not runnable from this runner.

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  D[workflow_dispatch provider] --> S[setup: Resolve provider]
  S -->|zai default| Z["zai glm-5.3-flash (byte-identical)"]
  S -->|kimi-for-coding| K["kimi k3-256k + caps"]
  S -->|custom| C["validated provider-config JSON"]
  S -->|missing secret| E[::error in first minute]
  S --> O["outputs: type/config/key_env/bench_model/run_label"]
  O --> B["shard env: FA_PROVIDER_* + 3 key mappings"]
  B --> R["run block picks key by name (indirection)"]
  O --> M["job name + summary: BENCH_RUN_LABEL"]
```

</details>

# gh-1503: [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only

## Description

## Problem

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

Port the #1471 design onto `bench-harbor.yml`, reusing the exact same mapping (single source — extract the resolve step into a composite action or shared script if that kills the duplication; otherwise a byte-consistent copy with a cross-reference comment in both files):

1. `provider` choice input (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`) + `provider-config` for custom — same semantics, same validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-looking fields, jq-parse hard-fail).
2. kimi maps to type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384, key env from `secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`.
3. Preflight: selected provider's secret missing → fail in the first minute (today only the zai key is checked at :264).
4. Run identity: workflow/job names + summary carry provider+model (bench.yml pattern: `fa bench · <provider> · <model>`); the free-text `model` input becomes derived-from-provider (keep it as override only for `custom`, or drop it if redundant).
5. REG: default dispatch (no provider input) resolves byte-identical to today's zai glm wiring.
6. `n-concurrent` default is 1 ("z.ai rate-limit safe") — keep for zai; document the kimi-safe value in the input description (kimi coding plan tolerates more; owner picks at dispatch).

## Acceptance

- `bench-harbor.yml` dispatchable with `provider=kimi-for-coding`; smoke run (one task, e.g. the family smoke per docs/bench.md) green on TB 2.1 with kimi.
- actionlint + the workflow-shape tests extended for the new inputs/mapping (mirror of #1475's tests).
- Default-path REG green.

## References

- #1471 (design), PR #1475 (bench.yml implementation to mirror)
- bench-harbor.yml:247-264 (current hardcode)
- kimi wiring precedent: ~/.fah/config.yaml custom providers (apiType kimi, k3-256k)

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      # gh-1503: bench-harbor.yml carries a byte-consistent copy of this
      # step's run block (same inputs, same outputs) — keep both in sync;
      # the cross-reference comment in both files is the sync contract.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}

          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

  bench:
    name: fa on tbench ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench agent caps
    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    env:
      FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
      DATASET: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      # The optional self-hosted runner is a macOS box: setup-python cannot
      # write the hosted tool cache there (mkdir /Users/runner denied) and the
      # runner's own python3 is 3.14 — typer-based CLIs (harbor) break on 3.14.
      # The uv-managed CPython 3.13 user-space install below works on BOTH
      # runner kinds (the ubuntu-latest default included); uv is also the
      # canonical harbor install per the 4.0 docs.
      - name: Install harbor (uv-managed python 3.13)
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          uv venv --python 3.13 .bench-venv
          uv pip install --python .bench-venv/bin/python 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
          .bench-venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print("venv python:", sys.version.split()[0])'

      - name: Run harbor (fa agent, ${{ matrix.env }} env)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/harbor_fa
          # gh-1503: the provider triple is resolved once in the setup
          # job (preflighted secret + hard fail on an unmapped choice) —
          # the shard only consumes it. All three bench keys are mapped
          # here (custom's AC 2a: key only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY); the
          # run block picks the resolved one by name, fa_agent.py ships
          # exactly that key into the container.
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_type }}
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_config }}
          FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_key_env }}
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_ID: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_ID }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET }}
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          NCONC: ${{ inputs.n-concurrent }}
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py); absent inputs stay byte-for-byte
          # today's run (REG-1). A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # Pinned --job-name: one jobs/<name>/ dir per shard, so the summary
          # job's downloads cannot collide on harbor's timestamped default.
          # The family label keys results per dataset version (fa-4.0-*
          # matches the historical 4.0 names exactly).
          .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
            -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
            --job-name "fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${{ matrix.kind }}-${{ matrix.i }}" -o jobs \
            "${args[@]}"

      - name: Upload harbor job (shard ${{ matrix.i }})
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: harbor-job-shard-${{ matrix.i }}
          path: jobs/

      - name: Upload to Harbor Hub
        if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''
        env:
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          for job_dir in jobs/fa-${FAMILY}-*; do
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor upload "$job_dir" --public
          done

  summary:
    name: Aggregate resolution rate
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs

          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1503` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +713
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:10:58Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:35:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #1503
## What changed

Ported the gh-1471 provider selection onto `bench-harbor.yml` (TB 2.x/Harbor path): a setup-job **Resolve provider** step maps the new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom` + `provider-config`) to the full provider triple and preflights the selected secret before any shard starts. The free-text `model` input is dropped — the model is derived from the provider.

## Key decisions

- **Byte-consistent copy, not extraction**: the resolve step's `run:` block is byte-identical to `bench.yml`'s (verified by a test); cross-reference comments in both files are the sync contract (single-source extraction was rejected to keep the workflows self-contained, same call gh-1471 made).
- **REG-1**: default dispatch resolves the exact 3-field zai JSON the workflow hardcoded pre-change (pinned in tests).
- **kimi** maps to type `kimi`, `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000 / maxTokens 16384, key from `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`; `custom` gets the full gh-1471 validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-like fields at any depth, Dart preconfig contract mirror).
- **Run identity**: `run-name: fa bench-harbor · <provider> · <tasks>`, shard job name carries `run_label`, summary gets `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` (`bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` gained the gh-1471-style `Provider:` line).
- **Defense in depth**: shard run block resolves the key by name via `FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV` indirection (same as bench.yml).
- `n-concurrent` default stays `1`; the kimi-safe guidance lives in the input description.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa   # 58 tests, incl. the mirrored resolve-block suite
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench  # 345 tests, bench.yml REG green
actionlint .github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml  # only 3 pre-existing findings (inputs.model one fixed)
```

Note: live smoke (`provider=kimi-for-coding`, one 2.1 family smoke task, `attempts: 1`) still requires the `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret and a real dispatch — not runnable from this runner.

# gh-1503: [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only

## Description

## Problem

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

Port the #1471 design onto `bench-harbor.yml`, reusing the exact same mapping (single source — extract the resolve step into a composite action or shared script if that kills the duplication; otherwise a byte-consistent copy with a cross-reference comment in both files):

1. `provider` choice input (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`) + `provider-config` for custom — same semantics, same validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-looking fields, jq-parse hard-fail).
2. kimi maps to type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384, key env from `secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`.
3. Preflight: selected provider's secret missing → fail in the first minute (today only the zai key is checked at :264).
4. Run identity: workflow/job names + summary carry provider+model (bench.yml pattern: `fa bench · <provider> · <model>`); the free-text `model` input becomes derived-from-provider (keep it as override only for `custom`, or drop it if redundant).
5. REG: default dispatch (no provider input) resolves byte-identical to today's zai glm wiring.
6. `n-concurrent` default is 1 ("z.ai rate-limit safe") — keep for zai; document the kimi-safe value in the input description (kimi coding plan tolerates more; owner picks at dispatch).

## Acceptance

- `bench-harbor.yml` dispatchable with `provider=kimi-for-coding`; smoke run (one task, e.g. the family smoke per docs/bench.md) green on TB 2.1 with kimi.
- actionlint + the workflow-shape tests extended for the new inputs/mapping (mirror of #1475's tests).
- Default-path REG green.

## References

- #1471 (design), PR #1475 (bench.yml implementation to mirror)
- bench-harbor.yml:247-264 (current hardcode)
- kimi wiring precedent: ~/.fah/config.yaml custom providers (apiType kimi, k3-256k)
